newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria's parliament puts off crisis debate.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria's parliament puts off crisis debate.

text.p: Bulgaria's parliament, besieged by protesting demonstrators, on Friday put off holding an extraordinary debate on an opposition-sponsored "salvation declaration" which would lead to early parliamentary elections.

Parliament, where the ruling Socialists have a majority, voted against holding an extraordinary session by 89 to 46 with 58 abstaining. The vote took place amid the stench of tear gas as riot police tried to keep out opposition supporters who broke into the building earlier.
Parliament speaker Blagovest Sendov was meeting with heads of parliamentary groups to discuss the crisis.

Dozens of riot police clashed with demonstrators inside the building and tried to disperse them with hoses and tear gas. They also used teargas to try to disperse hundreds of opposition supporters who formed a human chain around parliament.
Opposition UDF deputies had walked out of parliament after the ruling Socialists rejected the vote on the "salvation declaration" earlier on Friday.
The opposition says the Bulgarian Socialist Party has failed to tackle the country's economic crisis and now lacks support to form a government.
